title: 'What does it mean to catch students learning with AI?'
author: Lance Eaton
source: AI+Edu=Simplified (Substack), interview with Christine R. Rodriguez, August 4, 2026
summary: In an interview, Fairfield University biology professor Christine R. Rodriguez describes how she builds AI into clinical nursing and biology courses: modeled prompts, a bubonic-plague role-play exercise, and an LMS-based 'AI Conversations' tool where students practice explaining medical information to a simulated patient. She argues for flipping the surveillance mindset around AI in education — from catching students cheating to catching them genuinely learning — while walking students through both the practical value and real limitations of the technology.
points: Rodriguez has students role-play as caregivers across different historical eras of the bubonic plague, using AI as one of several research tools, to teach how scientific understanding evolves.
An LMS tool called 'AI Conversations' lets nursing students practice explaining medical information to an AI acting as a patient, then reflect on what they learned.
She models effective prompting explicitly as a disciplinary skill, teaching what a 'too general vs. specific' prompt looks like within biology.
In a non-majors 'BioInspiration' course, students hold AI Conversations with an organism (a sunflower, a kingfisher) to explore biomimicry in engineering design.
Her core reframe: 'Instead of centering the conversation on catching students cheating with AI, I keep trying to hold the mindset of: What does it mean to catch students learning with AI?'
quotes: Instead of centering the conversation on catching students cheating with AI, I keep trying to hold the mindset of: What does it mean to catch students learning with AI?
